title: Don Byas of Muskogee
summary: Fields foresaw Byas' success; Love recalls rooming with him in Basie's band in 1943 and his later life in Europe.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Now, Don Byas worked in your band?
Yes, now Don Byas didn't work in the band too much after he was just sure enough things were going, but Don Byas and I broke bread together. You see, Don

Byas was from Muskogee, that's his home, and that's only sixty miles from Tulsa and then all of those youngsters around there want to say that they made a few dates with me, and terrific, I saw his talent from the beginning and he was great and I predicted that he would be one of the big ones and he sure did turn out to be.
Don and I worked briefly with Basie in 1943, we roomed together in fact. He was one of the great saxophonists. Did you know how he died?
He died in Austria, I think it was, he was a mailman. He got to drinking very badly and I don't think they were hiring him much, but he was a postman.
It's just so bad how the whiskey messes up so many.
Don got onto that badly. Of course, he was an ex-patriot living in Europe for thirty years practically; he never came back
to the United States but once after many years in Europe.
